Subject: Recap: inference economics & operational constraints — next decision windows

Sara — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned.

Key pain points we heard:
- Latency spikes across your peak auth flows (p95 ~220–300ms today) causing checkout drop-offs.
- Token spend growth risk: current LLM volume trajectory would push monthly inference spend >20% of your ML infra budget by Q1 if unoptimized.
- Strict data residency / audit requirements for AML checks; procurement prefers customer-managed network/VPC.

Goals you stated:
- Pilot to prove 50% cost reduction vs current baseline without degrading end-user latency (target p95 <120ms for LLM calls).
- 3-month pilot window, production-like traffic (auth + support routing).
- Clear SLOs (latency, error rate) and audit logs for compliance.

Redwood levers & immediate recommendations (TCO focus):
1) Batching & KV cache: prefix caching + request-side batching anticipated to cut token compute by ~25–40% on your auth flow mix.
2) Quantization profile: 8-bit quantization for generator model variants — lowers GPU memory and enables cheaper instance classes; tradeoff: run small eval to confirm quality.
3) Routing policy: host latency-critical traffic on a low-latency pool (dedicated or region pin) and route lower-priority queries to cost tier.
4) Pilot sizing: start with a single dedicated shard sized to your 95th percentile concurrency estimate (we used your Q3 sample to estimate).

ROI framing (back-of-envelope):
- If caching/batching hit 30% and quantization gives a further 20% token-cost reduction, unit inference cost could drop ~44%.
- For your projected 12M tokens/month auth baseline, that is roughly $Xk/month savings (see attached workbook for the math and sensitivity to p95 and batch size).

Immediate asks / next steps (proposed timeline):
1) You: share a 2-week traffic sample CSV and the data residency checklist (by Fri 10/16) — we’ll use to finalize pilot sizing.
2) Redwood: deliver a pilot scope doc + itemized estimate (attached) and a draft SOW for procurement review (by Tue 10/20).
3) Joint: 30-minute technical kickoff to lock network modes (hosted vs private VPC) — propose Wed 10/21 10:00am PT.

Attachments: fintegro-traffic-sample-q3.csv (placeholder), redwood-pilot-scope-estimate-v1.pdf, pilot-pricing-workbook.xlsx

If any of this is off-base, tell me and I’ll update. Otherwise we’ll move forward to the SOW and procurement packet.

Best,
Jonas
